title: The rectangle passes to the derived limit
statement:
Use the four corner towers $A_\bullet,B_\bullet,C_\bullet,D_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(Y'))$ and the compatible morphisms $h:A_\bullet\to B_\bullet$, $v:A_\bullet\to C_\bullet$, $h':C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$, $v':B_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ of [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility]. Fix the triangulated derived-limit functor $F=\Rlim$ of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality], with its natural Roos triangles [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle], and put
$$
 A_\infty=F(A_\bullet),\quad B_\infty=F(B_\bullet),\quad C_\infty=F(C_\bullet),\quad D_\infty=F(D_\bullet).
$$
Let $H=F(h)$, $V=F(v)$, $H'=F(h')$, $V'=F(v')$. Then
$$
 V'H=H'V:A_\infty\longrightarrow D_\infty.
$$
For any one of these towers $M_\bullet$, let $\operatorname{pr}_{M,n}:M_\infty\to M_n$ be the first map of its natural Roos triangle followed by the $n$-th product projection. For every $n\geq1$, the component assertion means precisely
$$
 \operatorname{pr}_{D,n}V'H
 =v'_nh_n\operatorname{pr}_{A,n}
 =h'_nv_n\operatorname{pr}_{A,n}
 =\operatorname{pr}_{D,n}H'V.
$$

note:
*Source note:* the assertion is the functoriality of the derived limit of
Stacks Project, Derived Categories, Definition 13.34.1 ([Tag
08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC)), whose triangle is natural
in the system, so that a functorial model of $\Rlim$ carries compatible
tower morphisms to morphisms and preserves composition. The Stacks entry
states the triangle for one system; the blueprint adds the assembly over the
tower category, the functoriality of the sequential derived inverse limit
proved above, and the identification of the $n$-th components of both sides
with the finite-level equations $v'_nh_n=h'_nv_n$.

proof.text: The tower-compatibility statement gives the four arrows in a single derived tower category and its commuting rectangle $v'h=h'v$. Applying the functor $F$ of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] to this equality, and using preservation of composition, gives $V'H=F(v'h)=F(h'v)=H'V$. The equality is proved in the derived category itself, without inferring it from its components.

proof.text: For a tower arrow $a:M_\bullet\to N_\bullet$, write $a_n=\operatorname{ev}_n(a)$. naturality of the Roos triangle in [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] gives $p_NF(a)=(R\!\prod_n a_n)p_M$, where $p_M:M_\infty\to R\!\prod_n M_n$ is its first arrow. The defining identity of the product map is $\pi_{N,n}(R\!\prod_k a_k)=a_n\pi_{M,n}$. Thus composing the naturality identity with that projection gives $\operatorname{pr}_{N,n}F(a)=a_n\operatorname{pr}_{M,n}$. Applying this identity first to $v'$ and then to $h$ gives $\operatorname{pr}_{D,n}V'H=v'_nh_n\operatorname{pr}_{A,n}$; applying it first to $h'$ and then to $v$ gives $\operatorname{pr}_{D,n}H'V=h'_nv_n\operatorname{pr}_{A,n}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility], evaluation of the tower rectangle gives $v'_nh_n=h'_nv_n$, proving the middle equality and hence the stated component formula. These are maps from $A_\infty$ to $D_n$, not evaluations of maps between derived-limit objects.
